entradas.text: I had a meeting scheduled with Paskal to receive the annual healthcare report.
He arrived at my office with stacks of papers underneath both arms.
“Mr. President.”
“Yeah...maybe.”
entradas.menu: “Yeah...maybe.”

entradas.text: “I know this seems like a lot.”
He put the mountain of papers on my desk. It made a loud thud sound.
“That sounds...just great.”
entradas.menu: “That sounds...just great.”

entradas.text: “Very well. Thanks for bringing these in.”
entradas.menu: “Very well. Thanks for bringing these in.”

entradas.text: “Reviewing it shouldn't take more than a day.”
He measured the pile again.
“Or maybe two.”
“No problem at all.”
“They contain very important information about the status of our healthcare.”
“Salaries, expenditures, hospital reports...whatever you like.”
“We can go through this together.”
“Please...no.”
entradas.menu: “Please...no.”

entradas.text: “Can't you just summarize?”
entradas.menu: “Can't you just summarise?”

entradas.text: “Okay. Let's begin.”
entradas.menu: “Okay. Let's begin.”

entradas.text: “But I don't want to bore you. So I will quickly summarize.”
He continued.
I breathed a sigh of relief as he put on his reading glasses to look at the document he was holding.
“So, we have concluded our report for the year.”
“We have more patients treated, less waiting times and higher treatment quality than the years before.”
“We have missed several funding opportunities to expand our services in the country, leading to several issues being unsolved.”
“We are certainly on the right path to challenge even Lespia or Valgsland in the matter but we are not there yet.”
“I couldn't agree more. The foundations we laid so far will influence the years to come.”
“There can't be a more valiant aim. The foundations we laid so far will influence the years to come.”
“The service quality has dropped across the country. We have longer waiting times, fewer doctors and nurses, and more areas without proper healthcare.”
“Thanks to the allocated funds from the state, we have improved the healthcare in the country overall. I have used the resources to begin a comprehensive health reform.”
“Our services haven't necessarily gotten better compared to the last years.”
“The health services have been downsized and cut according to the new budget plan which caused a negative impact.”
“That is great to hear. Thank you for your hard work, Paskal.”
entradas.menu: “That is great to hear. Thank you for your hard work, Paskal.”

entradas.text: “Just as I expected. It was a good decision to spend the budget on the healthcare.”
entradas.menu: “Just as I expected. It was a good decision to spend the budget on the healthcare.”

entradas.text: “Good. Under my Presidency, I want Sordish people to have the best health service they can get.”
entradas.menu: “Good. Under my Presidency, I want Sordish people to have the best health service they can get.”

entradas.text: “This wouldn't be possible without your wise decision, Mr. President. So, thank you.”
“However, give it a few more years and we might even surpass them.”
“We need to get to the level of superpowers.”
entradas.menu: “We need to get to the level of superpowers.”

entradas.text: “We can't simply follow the footsteps of other nations.”
entradas.menu: “We can't simply follow the footsteps of other nations.”

entradas.text: “No, Paskal. We *will* surpass them.”
entradas.menu: “No, Paskal. We *will* surpass them.”

entradas.text: “Yes! We will.”
“I agree. We need to pave our own path to a better healthcare for our citizens.”
“It will take effort. However, if we can stay for another term, I am sure we will.”
“Moving on...”
“Our privatization efforts had both positive and negative effects.”
“It helped us raise further funds that we spent on improving the system. Privatized hospitals opened in many places with top notch equipment.”
“But, on the other hand, privatized hospitals are rather expensive even for an ordinary middle-class citizen.”
“We should be able to serve all of our citizens without distinction.”
entradas.menu: “We should be able to serve all of our citizens without distinction.”

entradas.text: “These are the expected growing pains of our healthcare system.”
entradas.menu: “These are the expected growing pains of our healthcare system.”

entradas.text: “There are still public hospitals for lower-class citizens.”
entradas.menu: “There are still public hospitals for lower-class citizens.”

entradas.text: “One of the side effects of a privatised healthcare system.”
“We are doing that now thanks to the increased resources. However, there is still some disparity in terms of quality.”
“True. But, there is still some disparity in terms of quality.”
“I agree. Now, we need to look into the future.”
Paskal skimmed the rest of the document before putting it down.
“Anybody can succeed when given all the resources. We need to do better.”
entradas.menu: “Anybody can succeed when given all the resources. We need to do better.”

entradas.text: “Don't blame yourself. It was my decision.”
entradas.menu: “Don't blame yourself. It was my decision.”

entradas.text: “Then you need to do a better job, Paskal.”
entradas.menu: “Then you need to do a better job, Paskal.”

entradas.text: “Yes. I agree. The recession absolutely pushed welfare to the brink and no further funds mean we couldn't do much.”
“We are in this together, Mr. President. The Ministry is trying to improve the efficiency where possible even in this situation. I assure you.”
“Yes, Mr. President. I will do my best even in these circumstances.”
“But as you can see, it hasn't been the best year for us at all.”
“We will do better next year. Don't worry.”
entradas.menu: “We will do better next year. Don't worry.”

entradas.text: “Then get to the bottom of it.”
entradas.menu: “Then get to the bottom of it.”

entradas.text: “That is unfortunate but what is done is done.”
entradas.menu: “That is unfortunate but what is done is done.”

entradas.text: “I will do whatever I can.”
“That is what I am trying to achieve.”
“We should strive to do better in this avenue.”
“Try to keep the problems to a minimum as best you can.”
entradas.menu: “Try to keep the problems to a minimum as best you can.”

entradas.text: “During our next term we will re-evaluate the situation in health.”
entradas.menu: “During our next term we will re-evaluate the situation in health.”

entradas.text: “There were other priorities.”
entradas.menu: “There were other priorities.”

entradas.text: “We are overwhelmed. Cutting the expenditures overboard has put us in a spiral of losing further incomes due to the lack of quality health services.”
“We must. If we have another year like this one, we might not be able to recover fully. Ever.”
“I understand however, the health of our citizens should be closer to the top of that list.”
“My team is absolutely exhausted, and all the fired personnel from the Ministry are furious with our administration.”
“We let them down.”
“Sometimes sacrifices are necessary.”
entradas.menu: “Sometimes sacrifices are necessary.”

entradas.text: “We will assess the situation and find solutions.”
entradas.menu: “We will assess the situation and find solutions.”

entradas.text: “The situation is grave. We shouldn't underestimate it.”
“Yes, sure. But when one gets hit with the consequences of such sacrifices, it is hard to be happy about it.”
“We can't make everyone happy.”
entradas.menu: “We can't make everyone happy.”

entradas.text: “Perhaps. But, I understand where their dissatisfaction comes from.”
“Our new funds allowed us to build dozens of new hospitals around the country. We specifically focused on areas with a high demand of health services.”
“Great to hear that more citizens have access to hospitals.”
entradas.menu: “Great to hear that more citizens have access to hospitals.”

entradas.text: “The people will see clear progress in the new hospitals we built.”
entradas.menu: “The people will see clear progress in the new hospitals we built.”

entradas.text: “Good call.”
entradas.menu: “Good call.”

entradas.text: “Many citizens have already written letters to us, thanking for the new treatment possibilities and less waiting times.”
“Not just that, we have increased our overall bed count for patients which increased the treatment capacity in many hospitals.”
“Thank you. I try to do my best.”
“The quality of care increased due to the upgraded equipment and we were able to hire more healthcare staff.”
“Excellent, the people in the countryside deserve better health services.”
entradas.menu: “Excellent, the people in the countryside deserve better health services.”

entradas.text: “Inequality is our worst enemy and we are one step closer to beating it.”
entradas.menu: “Inequality is our worst enemy and we are one step closer to beating it.”

entradas.text: “Make sure they know that we were the ones who gave this to them.”
entradas.menu: “Make sure they know that we were the ones who gave this to them.”

entradas.text: “There is no need. They already know.”
“The disparity in services needs more effort to be completely solved. However, the additional funds for the rural areas are a great start.”
“Yes. They have been neglected for a long time due to political reasons. Not anymore.”
“The investments we poured into our rural health facilities has paid off greatly.”
“High morale and happiness will result in better service.”
entradas.menu: “High morale and happiness will result in better service.”

entradas.text: “The act was the first of its kind, along with the salary incentives in rural areas which resulted in more job applications to areas that lacked health staff.”
“Our doctors, nurses and other health workers deserved better.”
entradas.menu: “Our doctors, nurses and other health workers deserved better.”

entradas.text: “We are already seeing the positive results. It is safe to assume that it was worth it.”
“It better be worth the losses in capital.”
entradas.menu: “It better be worth the losses in capital.”

entradas.text: “The Ministry has been ecstatic about the changes. The departments have been singing your praises.”
“Surely. With the rural incentives we have more treatment quality in those areas as well.”
“The increase in salaries to all health workers was received very well.”
“All of these efforts have resulted in a clear improvement of access to health services for our citizens.”
“All these efforts have resulted in a clear increase of quality in health services provided to our citizens.”
He cleared his throat.
“Now that I have given you the short summary...”
“There is a very important matter to discuss.”
Leaning over to grab his briefcase, he pulled out a tan colored package. The package was stamped with big red letters that read 'Confidential'.
Paskal opened the package and brought out a few documents. He handed them over to me.
I took the documents from his hand.
entradas.menu: Take a look.

entradas.text: It was a report from the Ministry of Health. Each page had a stamp on it that read 'For The President's Eyes Only'.
The report was titled 'Polio Outbreak in Bergia'.
“How bad is it?”
entradas.menu: “How bad is it?”

entradas.text: “This is very concerning.”
entradas.menu: “This is very concerning.”

entradas.text: “It can't be that bad.”
entradas.menu: “It can't be that bad.”

entradas.text: “For now it seems to be under control. We have put a few villages under quarantine. The total number of infected is currently 1467. The death toll is at 23 so far.”
“If we have more outbreaks, the results will be terrible.”
“It is, Mr. President.”
“Do not underestimate diseases and plagues, Mr. President.”
“Thankfully we have received the additional funding to our healthcare.”
“This should curb the infection ratio. Although, I am afraid even that might not be enough.”
“We are not where we could have been in terms of our healthcare funding.”
“With what we currently have, I am afraid it might not be enough to curb the infection ratio.”
“With the funding cuts to our healthcare, we are in potentially very dangerous territory.”
“If the hospitals start overflowing, we will be done for.”
“I will tell it to you straight. With our current state, we can't even hope to curb the infection ration if there are more outbreaks.”
“This is a very serious matter, Mr. President. The lives of Sordish citizens are at stake.”
“What can we do about it?”
entradas.menu: “What can we do about it?”

entradas.text: “How bad can it be? Don't worry about it. It will stop. I know it.”
entradas.menu: “How bad can it be? Don't worry about it. It will stop. I know it.”

entradas.text: “I will do whatever it takes to eliminate this threat.”
entradas.menu: “I will do whatever it takes to eliminate this threat.”

entradas.text: “Mr. President. I beg you to see reason.”
“We have done our research.”
“With that attitude, I have no doubt that we will succeed.”
“But I'm afraid simply having the vaccines won't help. We need to make sure they are administered.”
“There is a cure. A vaccine was recently invented in United Contana, and the formula has been made available for free across the entire world.”
“No matter what people think about United Contana, if the same thing had happened in Arcasia, we would be paying a steep price for it.”
“Thanks to the very good decision made by you to increase funding for our healthcare, we have the capability to produce this vaccine locally.”
“Unfortunately, because of the state of our current funding, we have neither the required materials nor the capability to produce this vaccine locally.”
“Which means we have to buy it. It will be costly but nothing comes before health.”
“You are exaggerating. There have been fewer than 30 deaths and you said the infected were under quarantine. I'm not going to approve this procurement.”
entradas.menu: “You are exaggerating. There have been fewer than 30 deaths and you said the infected were under quarantine. I'm not going to approve this procurement.”

entradas.text: “Procure whatever you need. Immediately.”
entradas.menu: “Procure whatever you need. Immediately. [-1 Government Budget]”

entradas.text: “Mr. President. You are knowingly exposing Sordland to the dangers of this virus.”
“Polio doesn't distinguish. It can infect you, your daughter, your son, your wife. Think about them.”
“I beg you to reconsider.”
“We don't have enough funds. I already told you my decision.”
entradas.menu: “We don't have enough funds. I already told you my decision.”

entradas.text: “When you put it that way...Very well. Procure whatever you need.”
entradas.menu: “When you put it that way...Very well. Procure whatever you need. [-1 Government Budget]”

entradas.text: “Then may God save us all.”
“You will not regret this, Mr. President. I assure you.”
“You have once again proven that you are the right leader for Sordland in my eyes.”
“Right away, Mr. President.”
“This is a great first step.”
“We need to implement a nationwide mandatory Polio vaccination policy.”
“With your order, I can immediately get to work to ensure we are doing whatever it takes.”
“This might seem excessive however, it is absolutely necessary.”
“Whatever it takes to protect Sordland. Do it.”
entradas.menu: “Whatever it takes to protect Sordland. Do it.”

entradas.text: “Let's observe the situation first. We will be fine without it for now.”
entradas.menu: “Let's observe the situation first. We will be fine without it for now.”

entradas.text: “Very well. I will keep you up to date.”
“Excellent.”
“Now, if you will excuse me, I must get to work immediately.”
Paskal's shoulders dropped in defeat.
He got up from his seat.
“That was it for today, Mr. President.”
“I have done all I could.”
“Thank you for your time, Mr. President.”
He left my office, leaving me alone with a lot of paperwork to go through.
“Of course.”
“Thank you for your time, Mr. President.”
“Thanks to the allocated funds from privatization, we have improved the healthcare in the country overall. I have used the resources to begin a comprehensive health reform.”
